problems.problem: Point $O$ is the centre of the circle $c$ circumscribed about an acute triangle $ABC$. A circle $c'$ with centre $O'$ touches the circle $c$ at point $A$ and the side $BC$ at point $D$. The circle $c'$ intersects the lines $AB$ and $AC$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively, and the lines $OO'$ and $EO'$ at points $A'$ ($\neq A$) and $G$ ($\neq E$), respectively. The lines $BO$ and $A'G$ intersect at point $H$. Prove that $DF^2=AF\cdot GH$.

(a) Nine tiles; (b) sixteen tiles are glued to a wall as shown in the figure. In how many ways is it possible in case (a) to write on each tile one of the numbers $0$ or $1$ so that the product of the numbers on any two adjacent tiles (having a common side) is equal to $0$? In how many ways can this be done in case (b)?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/lithuaniatst_2008_p2_fig.png

Find all triples of positive integers $(x,y,z)$ satisfying the equality
$$1+4^x+4^y=z^2.$$

The equation
$$x^3+x^2=2^y+16$$
is given.
(A) Give any one pair $(x;y)$ of positive integer solutions $x$ and $y$ of this equation;
(B) Find all (remaining) pairs $(x;y)$ of positive integer solutions of this equation, if there are any, or prove that there are no more solutions.

An incomplete $2\times 2$ square made of three unit squares is called a corner, and a rectangle that can be assembled in the usual way (without gaps and without overlaps) from such corners is called successful. For example, the $2\times 3$ rectangle is successful, since it is made of two such corners.
(A) Is the $6\times 3$ rectangle successful?
(B) Is the $9\times 3$ rectangle successful?
(C) Give all possible dimensions of successful rectangles.

In triangle $ABC$ the angle $\angle A$ equals $30^\circ$, and the points $S$ and $I$ are the centres of its circumscribed and inscribed circles, respectively. On the sides $BA$ and $CA$, respectively, points $D$ and $E$ are marked such that
$$BD=CE=BC.$$
Prove that $SI$ is perpendicular and equal to $DE$.

Find all solutions in real numbers $a,b,c,d$ and $e$ of the system of equations
$$\begin{cases} a^2=b^3+c^3\\ b^2=c^3+d^3\\ c^2=d^3+e^3\\ d^2=e^3+a^3\\ e^2=a^3+b^3 \end{cases}$$

Point $I$ is the centre of the circle inscribed in triangle $ABC$, in which $AB\neq AC$. The lines $BI$ and $CI$ intersect the sides $AC$ and $AB$ of the triangle at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. What could be the measure of the angle $BAC$ of the triangle for which $DI=EI$?

What is the smallest value that the expression
$$x^2+y^2+z^2$$
can take, if $x$, $y$ and $z$ are real numbers such that
$$x^3+y^3+z^3-3xyz=1?$$

An $8\times 8$ square is divided into $64$ unit squares. Each unit square contains either the number $1$ or the number $-1$. In the resulting table of numbers, the sum of the four numbers of any $2\times 2$ square equals either $2$ or $-2$. Prove that the table contains two rows in which the same numbers are written in the same order.

Positive numbers $(a,b,c)$ satisfy the inequality
$$(a+b+c)\left(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}\right)<5+3\sqrt{2}.$$
Prove that $(a,b,c)$ are the sides of an acute triangle.

The sides of a scalene triangle $ABC$ satisfy the equality $AB=(AC+BC)/2$. Its medians intersect at point $M$, and its angle bisectors at point $I$. The lines $AM$ and $BI$ intersect at point $P$, and the lines $BM$ and $AI$ at point $Q$. Prove that the line $PQ$ passes through the midpoint of the segment $IM$.

On the diagonal $AC$ and the side $BC$ of a rhombus $ABCD$, points $M$ and $N$ are marked, respectively, such that $DM=MN$. The lines $AC$ and $DN$ intersect at point $P$, and the lines $AB$ and $DM$ at point $R$. Prove that $RP=PD$.

Find all triples of positive integers $(x,y,u)$ satisfying the system of equations
$$\begin{cases} x+y=u+12,\\ x^5+y^5=u^5+12. \end{cases}$$

A function $f$ is defined on the set of real numbers and takes real values. Prove that there exist real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that
$$f(x-f(y))>yf(x)+x.$$

Each participant of a chess tournament played two games against each other participant: one with the white pieces and the other with the black pieces. A won game is worth one point, a drawn game half a point, and a lost game $0$ points. At the end of the tournament all chess players had the same number of points.
(a) Prove that some two participants of the tournament drew the same number of games.
(b) Prove that some two participants of the tournament lost the same number of games playing with the white pieces.

Non-negative real numbers $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{100},x_{101},x_{102}$, where $x_{101}=x_1$ and $x_{102}=x_2$, satisfy the inequalities
$$x_i+x_{i+1}+x_{i+2}\le 1\quad\text{for every } i=1,2,\dots,100.$$
Find the largest possible value of the expression
$$x_1x_3+x_2x_4+x_3x_5+\dots+x_{99}x_{101}+x_{100}x_{102}.$$

The angle bisectors of an acute triangle $ABC$ intersect at point $I$, and its altitudes at point $H$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the shorter arc $AC$ of the circle circumscribed about the triangle. Find the angle $ABC$ if it is known that $MI=MH$.

Distinct positive integers $s_1,s_2,\dots,s_n$ satisfy the equality
$$\left(1-\frac{1}{s_1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{s_2}\right)\cdots\left(1-\frac{1}{s_n}\right)=\frac{51}{2010}.$$
What is the smallest possible value of $n$?

Points $A_0,B_0,C_0$ are the midpoints of the sides $BC,CA,AB$ of triangle $ABC$, respectively, and points $A_1,B_1,C_1$ bisect (by length) the broken lines $BAC,CBA,ACB$, respectively. Prove that the lines $A_0A_1$, $B_0B_1$, $C_0C_1$ are concurrent.

Positive integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{14}$, all greater than $4$, are given. We write on a board the $196$ (not necessarily distinct) sums $a_n+a_m$, where $1\le n,m\le 14$. Then in each sum we erase all digits except the last two. Is it possible that all possible two-digit combinations $00,01,\dots,98,99$ remain written on the board?

Triangle $ABC$ is acute. Points $B_1$ and $C_1$ are the feet of the altitudes of the triangle drawn from vertices $B$ and $C$, respectively. Points $P$ and $Q$ are given such that $B_1$ and $C_1$ are interior points of the segments $BP$ and $CQ$, respectively. The angle $PAQ$ is right. Point $F$ is the foot of the altitude of triangle $APQ$ drawn from vertex $A$. Prove that the angle $BFC$ is right.

Positive numbers $x,y,z$ satisfy the equality $x+y^2+z^3=1$. Prove that
$$\frac{x}{2+xy}+\frac{y}{2+yz}+\frac{z}{2+zx}>\frac{1}{2}.$$

For every integer $m$, denote by $f(m)$ the largest cube of an integer not exceeding $m$. For example, $f(26)=8$ and $f(27)=27$. A sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ is given, where $a_{n+1}=3a_n-2f(a_n)$ for every $n\ge 1$.
(a) Find at least one value of the first term $a_1$ in the interval $[2012,3000]$ for which there exists a number $M$ (depending only on $a_1$) such that $a_n\le M$ for every $n\ge 1$.
(b) Find all possible positive integer values of the first term $a_1$ for which there exists a number $M$ (depending only on $a_1$) such that $a_n\le M$ for every $n\ge 1$.
Six points are given inside a rectangle with sides $4$ and $5$. Prove that the distance between some two of the points is less than $3$.

The set of positive integers is partitioned into $k$ disjoint subsets $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k$ such that, for every positive integer $n\ge 15$, each of these $k$ subsets contains two distinct numbers whose sum equals $n$.
(a) Prove that the set of positive integers can be partitioned into three such subsets.
(b) Prove that the set of positive integers cannot be partitioned into $k$ such subsets if $k\ge 4$.

The diagonals of a rectangle $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. Point $E$ lies on the line $AB$ and $AE=AO$ (here point $A$ lies between points $E$ and $B$). Point $F$ lies on the line $DB$ and $BF=BO$ (here $B$ lies between $F$ and $D$). Triangle $EFC$ is equilateral. Prove that the line $EO$ is perpendicular to the line $DB$.

Positive integers $a,b,c$ and $d$ are such that $ac+bd$ is divisible by $a^2+b^2$. Can the greatest common divisor of the numbers $a^2+b^2$ and $c^2+d^2$ be equal to:
(a) $1$?
(b) $3$?
(c) $74$?

On some cells of a $12\times 12$ board there sits one beetle each. Two beetles are called neighbours if they are on cells having a common side or a common corner. What is the largest number of beetles that can sit on the board if each beetle has exactly one neighbour?
Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that if $P(m)$ is an integer, then $m$ is also an integer.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ (with $AB>AC$), the foot of the perpendicular dropped from the intersection point of the medians to the side $BC$ is point $D$. Find the ratio $BD:BA$ if $AD$ is the bisector of angle $BAC$.

A quadruple $(x,y,z,n)$, where $x,y,z$ are positive real numbers and $n$ is a positive integer, is called perfect if
$$\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}+\sqrt{z}=1$$
and $\sqrt{x+n}+\sqrt{y+n}+\sqrt{z+n}$ is an integer.
(a) Find at least one perfect quadruple $(x,y,z,n)$ with $n>2013$.
(b) Find all perfect quadruples $(x,y,z,n)$.

A circle touches the sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CD$ of a parallelogram $ABCD$ at points $K$, $L$ and $M$, respectively. A perpendicular is drawn from vertex $C$ to $AB$. Prove that the line $KL$ bisects this perpendicular.

A finite set $A$ has the following property: the sum of any $6$ distinct elements of it is not divisible by $6$.
(a) Find at least one such set $A$ consisting of $10$ distinct positive integers.
(b) Does there exist such a set $A$ consisting of $11$ distinct positive integers?

Positive real numbers $a,b$ and $c$ are given such that the system of equations
$$\begin{cases} a^2x+b^2y+c^2z=1,\\ xy+yz+zx=1 \end{cases}$$
has a unique real solution $(x,y,z)$. Prove that there exists a triangle with side lengths $a$, $b$ and $c$.

(a) Does there exist a positive integer $n$ such that the last digit of the number $2^n$ is $6$ and the sum of its other digits equals $2$?
(b) Do there exist positive integers $a$ and $m\ge 3$ such that the last digit of the number $a^m$ is $6$ and the sum of its other digits equals $3$?

Real numbers $x$ and $y$ are given. Denote $s_1=x+y$, $s_2=x^2+y^2$, $s_3=x^3+y^3$, $s_4=x^4+y^4$ and $t=xy$.
(a) Prove that the number $t$ is rational if $s_2$, $s_3$ and $s_4$ are rational numbers.
(b) Prove that the number $s_1$ is rational if $s_2$, $s_3$ and $s_4$ are rational numbers.
(c) Can the number $s_1$ be irrational if $s_2$ and $s_3$ are rational numbers?
(A real number $r$ is called rational if it can be written as the ratio $\frac{p}{q}$ of two integers $p$ and $q$, for example $\frac{3}{2}$, $-\frac{17}{3}$, $4$, $0$, etc. Otherwise, i.e. if $r$ cannot be expressed in this way, it is called irrational, for example $\sqrt{5}$.)

Circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ do not intersect. Their common external tangents $a$ and $b$ and a common internal tangent $c$ are drawn. The lines $a$, $b$ and $c$ touch the circle $\omega_1$ at points $A_1$, $B_1$ and $C_1$, respectively, and the circle $\omega_2$ at points $A_2$, $B_2$ and $C_2$, respectively. Prove that the ratio of the areas of triangles $A_1B_1C_1$ and $A_2B_2C_2$ is equal to the ratio of the radii of the circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$.

Two tangent circles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are given. A common tangent of the circles touches $\alpha$ and $\beta$ at (distinct) points $A$ and $B$, respectively. The segment $AP$ is a diameter of the circle $\alpha$, and a line passing through point $P$ touches $\beta$ at point $Q$. Prove that $AP=PQ$.

Find all positive integer solutions $(a,b,c)$ of the equation
$$a!\cdot b!=a!+b!+c!.$$
(Here $n!=1\cdot 2\cdot\ldots\cdot n$, for example $4!=1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot 4=24$.)

A $5\times 5$ table with cells that can light up is given. By touching cells one can change their state: switch off the lit ones and switch on again the unlit ones. When any cell is touched, the state changes not only of that cell but also of all cells adjacent to it (having a common side with it). Initially all cells of the table are switched off, and Hermina wants exactly one cell of the table to be lit. For example, if Hermina touched, in some order, the cells marked in the figure, she would switch on the single cell $A$, and all the other cells would remain switched off.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/lithuaniatst_2015_p3_fig.png

(a) Find four more cells that can become the single cell lit at the end.
(b) Prove that none of the remaining $20$ cells of the table can become the single cell lit at the end.

Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
$$f(x)f(y)=f(x+y)+xy$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.
(Here $\mathbb{R}$ denotes the set of all real numbers.)

Sets $A$ and $B$ are subsets of the set of positive integers $\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ having the following two properties:
(a) The sum $x+y$ of any two distinct elements $x$ and $y$ of the set $A$ belongs to the set $B$.
(b) The ratio $\frac{z}{t}$ of any two distinct elements $z$ and $t$ of the set $B$ (dividing the larger number $z$ by the smaller $t$) belongs to the set $A$.
What is the largest number of elements the union $A\cup B$ can have?
(The set $A\cup B$ consists of the elements belonging to at least one of the two sets $A$ and $B$.)
A parallelogram $ABCD$ with centre $S$ is given. The incircle of triangle $ABD$, with centre $O$, touches $BD$ at point $T$. Prove that the lines $OS$ and $CT$ are parallel.

A chess bishop can be moved in one move from one cell of an $8\times 8$ board to another if these cells lie on one diagonal. Thus a bishop can move in four directions. A piece called a shmikis moves like a bishop, but can move in only three of those four directions (the missing direction may differ for two shmikises). What is the largest number of shmikises that can be placed on an $8\times 8$ board so that no shmikis can capture another in one move?

Find all positive integer solutions $(a,b,c,d)$ of the equation
$$4^a\cdot 5^b-3^c\cdot 11^d=1.$$

The altitude $CK$ of an acute scalene triangle $ABC$ intersects the other two altitudes at point $H$. On the side $AB$ a point $D$ is marked such that the segment $CD$ passes through the centre $O$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of the segment $CD$. Prove that the line $EK$ bisects the segment $OH$.

The altitude $AD$ and the angle bisector $AL$ of triangle $ABC$ are drawn. Its circumcircle $\omega$ intersects the line $AL$ at point $M
eq A$, the line $MD$ at point $N
eq M$, and the line $NL$ at point $E
eq N$. Prove that $AE$ is a diameter of $\omega$.

An integer is written on each face of a cube. In a move it is allowed to choose any two adjacent faces and increase the numbers on them by $1$. After several moves all six numbers became equal. Determine for which initial collections of numbers this could have happened.

Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ for which the inequality
$$f(xy)\le xf(y)$$
holds for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.
(Here $\mathbb{R}$ denotes the set of all real numbers.)

On the sides $AB$ and $AC$ of triangle $ABC$, points $K$ and $N$ are marked, respectively, such that $KB=KN$. The bisector of angle $ACB$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at points $C$ and $R$. The perpendicular dropped from point $R$ to the line $AB$ intersects the segment $BN$ at point $D$. Prove that the points $A$, $K$, $D$ and $N$ lie on one circle.

A set consisting of $m\ge 2$ positive integers is called simple if any two elements of this set are coprime. Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that every simple set which is a subset of the set $S=\{1,2,\dots,2017\}$ and which has exactly $n$ elements always contains at least one prime number.

Two polynomials with integer coefficients $A(x)=a_nx^n+\dots+a_1x+a_0$ and $B(x)=b_mx^m+\dots+b_1x+b_0$ (here $m,n\ge 0$ and $a_n,b_m\neq 0$) are called similar if $m=n$ and every integer occurs the same number of times in the collections $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_n$ and $b_0,b_1,\dots,b_n$.
Polynomials with integer coefficients $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are similar and $P(16)=3^{2012}$.
(a) Prove that $Q(3^{2012})\neq 0$.
(b) Find the smallest possible value of $|Q(3^{2012})|$.

Primes $p>q$ and positive integers $k,\ell$ are given. The set $A$ consists of all positive integers $n$ for which $p^kq^\ell n$ is divisible by $p+n$.
(a) Prove that $|A|\ge 1$.
(b) Prove that $|A|\ge k\ell+k+\ell$.
(c) Prove that $|A|\le k\ell+k+2\ell-1$.
(d) Does there exist a pair of primes $p>q$ for which $|A|=127$ when $k=\ell=10$?
(Here $|A|$ denotes the number of elements of the set $A$.)

Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ for which the equality
$$f(xf(y)-yf(x))=f(xy)-xy$$
holds for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.
(Here $\mathbb{R}$ denotes the set of all real numbers.)

A positive integer $n\ge 4$ is given. A regular $n$-gon is divided into triangles by drawing $n-3$ non-intersecting (having no common interior points) diagonals. What is the largest number of pairwise non-congruent triangles that can be among the resulting ones?

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle. The rays $AB$ and $DC$ intersect at point $K$. The midpoints of the segments $AC$ and $CK$ are denoted by $M$ and $N$, respectively. The points $B,D,M,N$ lie on one circle. Find all possible values of $\angle ADC$.

Two positive integers $n\ge m\ge 2$ are given. Gitanas and Saulius play the following game. Gitanas must choose $m$ distinct numbers from the set $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. If Saulius can choose from these $m$ numbers two numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $a<b\le 2a$, then he wins the game. Otherwise, if there is no such pair $(a,b)$, Gitanas wins the game.
(a) Prove that Gitanas can win the game when $(n,m)=(66,6)$.
(b) Prove that Saulius can win the game, no matter how Gitanas plays, when $(n,m)=(2018,11)$.
(c) For every $m\ge 2$ find all values of $n$ for which Saulius can win the game, no matter how Gitanas plays.

Call a positive integer $n$ successful if there exist infinitely many collections of positive rational numbers $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for which both numbers $a_1+\dots+a_n$ and $\frac{1}{a_1}+\dots+\frac{1}{a_n}$ are positive integers. (For example, the number $n=1$ is not successful, since $a_1$ and $\frac{1}{a_1}$ are both positive integers if and only if $a_1=1$. The numbers $a_1,\dots,a_n$ need not be distinct.)
(a) Prove that the number $n=2$ is not successful.
(b) Prove that every positive integer $n\ge 3$ is successful.

For every odd positive integer $n$, determine the units digit of the number
$$\frac{10^{n(n+1)}}{10^n+6}.$$
(For example, the units digit of the number $27.83$ is $7$, and the units digit of the number $\pi=3.14\ldots$ is $3$.)

On the side $AB$ of a square $ABCD$ the midpoint $M$ is marked. The perpendicular dropped from point $B$ to the line $CM$ meets the line $CM$ at point $P$. Point $N$ is the midpoint of the segment $CP$. The bisector of angle $DAN$ and the line $DP$ intersect at point $Q$. Prove that the quadrilateral $BMQN$ is a parallelogram.

Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ for which the equality
$$(x+y)f(yf(x))=x^2(f(x)+f(y))$$
holds for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^+$.
(Here $\mathbb{R}^+$ denotes the set of all positive real numbers.)

Mykolas thought of a sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$, and then defined a new sequence $b_1,b_2,b_3,\dots$ by the equalities
$$b_1=a_1,\quad b_2=a_2,\quad b_n=a_nb_{n-1}+b_{n-2}\ \text{ for all } n\ge 3.$$
Could Mykolas have chosen the initial sequence $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ so that each of the numbers $b_1,b_2,b_3,\dots$ is
(a) the square of a positive integer?
(b) the cube of a positive integer?

The angle bisectors of triangle $ABC$ intersect at point $I$. Points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of the sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. The lines $MN$ and $CI$ intersect at point $P$. A point $Q$ is marked such that the lines $MN$ and $PQ$ are perpendicular, and the lines $BI$ and $NQ$ are parallel. Find the angle between the lines $AC$ and $IQ$.

Positive integers $m$ and $n$ are given. $12m$ participants came to a gathering of checkers players. During it each participant played exactly $3m+6$ games of checkers. Any two participants played each other at most once. For any two participants $A$ and $B$ of the gathering there are exactly $n$ other participants who played checkers with both $A$ and $B$. Find $m$ and $n$.

Circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ intersect at two points $A$ and $B$. Lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ pass through $B$ and intersect the circle $\omega_1$ at points $C$ and $E$, respectively, and the circle $\omega_2$ at points $D$ and $F$, respectively (here $C,E,D,F
eq B$). The line $CF$ intersects $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ at points $P
eq C$ and $Q
eq F$, respectively. The midpoints of the arcs $BP$ and $BQ$, lying inside $\omega_2$ and $\omega_1$ respectively, are denoted by $M$ and $N$, respectively. Prove that if $CD=EF$, then the points $C$, $F$, $M$, $N$ lie on one circle.

Call a positive integer $n$ five-divisible if it has five distinct positive divisors the sum of whose fourth powers equals $n$. (The numbers $1$ and $n$ are also divisors of $n$.)
(a) Prove that a five-divisible number is always divisible by $5$.
(b) Determine whether there are infinitely many five-divisible positive integers.

Find:
(a) the largest possible value of the expression
$$(1-x)(1-y)(1-xy)$$
when $x,y\in[-1;1]$;
(b) the largest possible value of the expression
$$(1-x)(1-y)(1-z)(1-xy)(1-yz)(1-xyz)$$
when $x,y,z\in[-1;1]$.

There are $4044$ weights whose masses (in grams) are $1,2,3,\dots,4044$. Agnė wants to choose $2022$ weights whose total mass is an even number. Benas claims: whatever weights Agnė chooses, he will be able to distribute them into two piles so that the masses of the two piles are equal. (The piles need not contain the same number of weights.) Is Benas right?

A triangle $ABC$ with $\angle BAC=60^\circ$ is given. On the extension of side $AB$ beyond vertex $B$ and on the extension of side $AC$ beyond vertex $C$, points $D$ and $E$ are marked, respectively, such that $BD=BC=CE$. The circumcircle of triangle $ACD$ intersects the segment $DE$ at point $P\neq D$. Prove that the segment $AP$ is the angle bisector of triangle $ADE$.

Determine all real numbers $c$ for which there exists a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
$$f(f(x)+f(y))+cxy=f(x+y)$$
for all real $x$ and $y$.

Prove that if $a,b$ and $c$ are positive real numbers, then
$$\frac{a^4b^4}{a^3+b^3}+\frac{b^4c^4}{b^3+c^3}+\frac{c^4a^4}{c^3+a^3}\le\frac{a^5+b^5+c^5}{2}.$$

For every positive integer $n\ge 3$ determine the largest possible value of the expression
$$x_1x_2+x_2x_3+\dots+x_{n-1}x_n+x_nx_1,$$
when $\{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n\}=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$.

Determine whether there exist $2003$ numbers
$$a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots,a_{2003}\in\{1,2,3,\dots,4006\}$$
such that $a_1<a_2<a_3<\dots<a_{2003}$ and the number
$$2^{a_1}+2^{a_2}+2^{a_3}+\dots+2^{a_{2003}}+2^{4007}$$
is divisible by $2004$.

Mikas wrote a finite sequence of integers $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$. Here $n\ge 1$, $a_n=0$, and the first $n$ terms of the sequence are greater than $1$. Mikas obtained each term $a_{i+1}$, for $i=0,1,2,\dots,n-1$, in turn by subtracting from the number $a_i$ the smallest prime divisor of $a_i$. For each number $k\in\mathbb{N}$, denote by $M(k)$ the set of all possible values of $a_0$ when $n=k$.
(a) Determine all elements of the set $M(386)$.
(b) Prove that there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ for which the set $M(k)$ has exactly $10$ elements.

Real numbers $x,y,z$ satisfy the conditions $0\le x<\frac{2z}{3}$, $0\le y<\frac{3}{2}$ and
$$z^2+y^2=1+x^2=(z-x)^2+(1-y)^2.$$
(a) Find at least one possible value of $z$.
(b) Find the largest possible value of $z$.

On the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of triangle $ABC$, points $D$ and $E$ are marked, respectively, such that $CD=CE$. The angle bisector from $A$ of triangle $ABC$ intersects the segment $DE$ at point $P$. The lines $AB$ and $DE$ intersect at point $F$ (point $B$ lies between $A$ and $F$). Prove that $AF\cdot BF+CP^2=CF^2$ if and only if $AD\cdot BE=DP^2$.

A circle passing through the midpoint $M$ of side $AC$ of triangle $ABC$ and tangent to the line $BC$ at point $B$ intersects the segment $AB$ at its interior point $P$. Prove that $AB\cdot BP=2BM^2$.

A positive integer $n$ is given. Auksė and Baltrus play the following game, making moves alternately. In a move a player must choose any of the numbers $1,2,3,4,5$ and write it on the board. Auksė makes the first move. The game ends when the two players have made $n$ moves in total. If the sum of the $n$ written numbers is divisible by $9$, Baltrus wins; otherwise Auksė wins. Determine all values of $n$ for which Auksė has a winning strategy.

For every positive integer $n$, denote by $A_n$ the set of the $n$-th powers $x^n$ of all positive rational numbers $x$ except the positive integers. Thus $A_n=\{x^n : x>0,\ x\in\mathbb{Q},\ x\notin\mathbb{N}\}$.
(a) Prove that for every odd $n\ge 3$ there are infinitely many integers that can be written as the sum of two distinct elements of the set $A_n$.
(b) Determine whether there exists an integer that can be written both as the sum of two distinct elements of the set $A_3$ and as the sum of the cubes of two distinct integers.
Determine the smallest value that the expression $x^2+y^2+z^2$ can take, when the real numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ satisfy the condition $xyz+x+y+z=xy+yz+zx+5$.

A triangle $ABC$ with $AB=15$, $BC=14$ and $AC=13$ is given. The segments $BM$ and $CN$ are its medians, and the segments $BD$, $CE$ are its angle bisectors. The circles circumscribed about triangles $ADE$ and $AMN$ intersect at point $P$ (here $P\neq A$). The line $AP$ intersects the line $BC$ at point $Q$. Find $BQ$.

$2n+1$ players (here $n\in\mathbb{N}$) took part in a tennis tournament. Before the tournament each of them had a certain rating. The ratings of all tennis players were distinct, and during the tournament, in which every player played one match against every other player, the ratings did not change. (There are no draws in tennis, so every match ended with the victory of one of the players.) There were exactly $k$ matches in the tournament in which the player with the lower rating won against the player with the higher rating, where $1\le k\le 2n^2+n$.
Prove that at least one player of the tournament won at least $n-\sqrt{2k}$ and at most $n+\sqrt{2k}$ of the matches he played.

Three piles contain $a$, $b$ and $c$ candies. Matas and Nora take turns making the following move: eat one pile of candies and divide one of the other piles into two non-empty piles. A player loses when he can no longer make a move, i.e. when each of the three piles has one candy left. Which player has a winning strategy when $(a,b,c)=(200,400,2024)$? (Matas starts the game.)

Denote by $P(n)$ the product of all primes dividing a positive integer $n>1$. (For example, $P(12)=P(2^2\cdot 3)=2\cdot 3=6$, and $P(7)=7$.) A pair of positive integers $(s,t)$ with $1<s<t$ is called friendly if $P(s)=P(t)$ and $P(s+1)=P(t+1)$.
(a) Find at least one friendly pair $(s,t)$ with $s\ge 10$.
(b) Does there exist at least one friendly pair $(s,t)$ with $s$ odd?
(c) Prove that there are infinitely many friendly pairs.

Suppose that $S$ is a finite set of non-zero numbers, and $f:S\to S$ is a function satisfying, for every $x\in S$, one of the equalities
$$f(f(x))=x+f(x)\quad\text{or}\quad f(f(x))=\frac{x+f(x)}{2}.$$
Prove that then $f(x)=x$ for every $x\in S$.

Each cell of a $7\times 7$ table contains one of the three numbers $-1$, $0$ and $1$. In the table, the sum of the nine numbers of every $3\times 3$ square equals $0$. The sum of all $49$ numbers equals $s$. Determine the largest possible value of $s$.

Determine all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ for which the equality
$$f(xf(x+y)+y)=f(x^2)+yf(x)+f(y)$$
holds for all real $x$ and $y$.

Similar triangles $ABE$ and $CFB$ are drawn outside a parallelogram $ABCD$ (here $\angle ABE=\angle CFB$, $\angle BAE=\angle FCB$). The lines $AD$ and $BF$ intersect at point $G$, and the lines $CD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $H$. Prove that the points $D$, $E$, $F$, $G$ and $H$ lie on one circle.

Positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfy the equality
$$(a+b+ab)(a+b-ab)=ab.$$
For each of the expressions $a+b+ab$ and $a+b-ab$ determine its smallest possible value.

The numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ are positive integers. When the three numbers $a^2+1$, $b^2+1$ and $c^2+1$ are divided by a common positive divisor, the numbers $x$, $x+3$ and $x+y$, respectively, are obtained. Determine which of the following values of $y$ are possible: (a) $y=2025$; (b) $y=99$; (c) $y=75$.

For every positive integer $a$, denote by $S(a)$ the sum of the digits of its decimal representation. Determine whether there exists a positive integer $m$ such that the number $S(mn)$ is even for every positive integer $n$.

The diagonals of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ intersect at point $M$. The circumcircles of triangles $ABM$ and $CDM$ intersect the line $BC$ at points $K\neq B$ and $L\neq C$, respectively. Points $P$ and $Q$ are the feet of the altitudes from vertex $M$ of triangles $AKM$ and $DLM$, respectively. Prove that the lines $BC$ and $PQ$ are parallel.

In a mathematical competition $30$ students solved $8$ problems. Afterwards, for each problem the number of students who solved it was determined. The number $a\ge 0$ of the remaining students (who did not solve that problem) is taken as the value of that problem, i.e. every student who solved that problem is awarded $a$ points for it. The remaining $a$ students are awarded $0$ points for that problem. For each student the total of all points he received is computed. The total of all points received by student $A$ is even.
(a) Is it possible that every student other than $A$ scored fewer points than $A$, but solved more problems than $A$?
(b) Is it possible that every student other than $A$ scored more points than $A$, but solved fewer problems than $A$?

Real numbers $a,b,c$ satisfy the equalities
$$a+b+c=0,\qquad a^2+b^2+c^2=10.$$
Determine the largest possible value of the expression
$$|(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)|.$$

A $5\times 5$ table, all $25$ cells of which are initially empty, and a positive integer $n$ are given. Players A and B make moves alternately; A makes the first move. In each move a player must choose a currently empty cell and write in it the number $1$ if the player is A, or the number $0$ if the player is B. After all $25$ cells are filled, for each of the nine $3\times 3$ squares the sum of all its nine numbers is computed, and the number $S$ is recorded: the one of the nine sums that none of the others exceeds. If $S\ge n$, A wins; otherwise B wins. Determine the largest possible value of $n$ for which player A has a winning strategy.

(a) Determine all positive integers $n>2$ for which there exists a sequence $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ in which each of the numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ occurs exactly once and for which the sum $a_1+a_2+\dots+a_k$ is divisible by $k$ for every $k=1,2,\dots,n$.
(b) Determine whether there exists an infinite sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ in which every positive integer occurs exactly once and for which the sum $a_1+a_2+\dots+a_k$ is divisible by $k$ for every positive integer $k$.
